content:
anya: hi team — i'm Anya, started today on runtime. trying to build from source (master) and hit a linker error during make: undefined reference to `__cudaRegisterFatBinary`. build step is GPU backend compile. anyone know who to flag or quick checks?

mohit: welcome! most likely a driver/toolkit mismatch. can you run `nvidia-smi` and `nvcc --version` and paste outputs? also share exact cmake/make commands you used.

anya: output below —
```
nvidia-smi
Tue Jun 17 13:04:12 2025
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| NVIDIA-SMI 535.54       Driver Version: 535.54       CUDA Version: 12.0     |
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+

nvcc: NVIDIA (R) Cuda compiler driver
Copyright (c) 2005-2024 NVIDIA Corporation
Built on Wed_Feb_14_21:00:00_PST_2024
Cuda compilation tools, release 12.0, V12.0.226

cmake .. -DUSE_CUDA=ON -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release
make -j8
```

mohit: ok, driver shows 535.x and cuda toolkit 12.0 — that should be compatible in general, but the undefined fatbinary error usually means the runtime linked against a different libcuda or the build picked up a mismatched nvcc. a couple quick things to try:
- run `ldconfig -p | grep libcudart` and `ldd build/bin/inference_runtime` to see missing libs.
- ensure `/usr/local/cuda` points to the same toolkit as `nvcc` (sometimes distro packages put a different version in /usr).
- clean out cmake cache: `rm -rf build && mkdir build && cd build` then re-run cmake pointing explicitly: `cmake .. -DUSE_CUDA=ON -DCUDA_TOOLKIT_ROOT_DIR=/usr/local/cuda-12.0`

maria: +1 to mohit. also for new hires we have a docker dev image that avoids host toolchain issues — ping @eng-infra if you need access to the internal image. onboarding doc: https://redwood-internal/docs/onboarding/runtime-builds (has docker run snippet). if you're on a laptop and using WSL/extra stuff, mention that.

ci-bot: runtime-ci: just a heads-up — nightly cuda-builder image was rebuilt at 2025-06-17T12:30Z (image: rwinf/runtime-cuda:2025-06-17). If you're using the old image, you might see mismatches.

noah: also check libcuda symlink and runtime loader: `ls -l /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libcuda.so*` and `sudo ldconfig`. sometimes drivers install libcudart into /usr/local/cuda-*/lib64 while system uses another path. run `ldd build/bin/inference_runtime | grep -i cuda` to confirm linked libs.

anya: tried the clean build + explicit CUDA_TOOLKIT_ROOT_DIR and `ldd` — it showed libcuda -> not found at first. i installed the cuda-toolkit apt package from nvidia (12.1) after seeing the image tag mismatch and now the linker error changed to a missing cudnn symbol.

mohit: missing cudnn symbol = cudnn version mismatch. check `ldconfig -p | grep cudnn` and confirm major versions. our runtime expects cudnn 8.x for cuda 12.1. if you installed an older lib from the package manager, install the corresponding libcudnn8 package.

anya: thanks — i installed libcudnn8 and now the binary links. ran `make -j8` again and compile passed. quick follow-up: where's the dev quickstart for the iterative debug workflow?

maria: good fix — dev quickstart is in the onboarding doc I linked. tl;dr: prefer using the nightly runtime-cuda image for day-to-day, set `DEV_CONTAINER=1` in your env, and use `./scripts/dev_run.sh --cuda` to get the right mounts and envs. ping @noah or @mohit if the image doesn't work for you. :tada:

anya: awesome, thanks everyone! tagging this resolved for my first-day checklist. will DM if i hit anything else.
